name: Rhythm — Constant Pulsating (Flutter Mode)
summary: Move so fast that individual strokes blur into a flutter—maintaining unbroken contact and steady pressure while micro-movements create a vibrator-like pulsation at the skin surface.
detailed_description: Also called flutter mode. The hand, tongue, or toy vibrates back and forth with each stroke barely completing before the next begins. Physical contact never breaks; pressure stays relatively constant while rapid oscillation sends ripple-like sensation through the contact point. OMGYES testimonials describe using this from start to finish for partners who want one sustained wave of stimulation rather than separated beats.
stepwise_structure: 1. Establish comfortable contact on the chosen area (often hood or glans, depending on sensitivity).
2. Flutter rapidly back and forth—small amplitude, high frequency—without lifting off between cycles.
3. Keep pressure steady; let speed and micro-motion do the work rather than pressing harder.
4. Sustain the flutter through a phase or the full session if that matches the receiver's preference.
5. Ease off gradually rather than stopping abruptly if sensitivity spikes.
safety_notes: Flutter on bare glans can be too intense for some—consider hood layering or lighter pressure.
Fatigue in hand or jaw (if oral) limits duration; switch hands or rhythm if needed.
Stop if burning, numbness, or oversensitivity occurs.
